title: A message set for a later day says 'Sent' at once, and its WhatsApp copies are handed over straight away
what: When the owner picks a later day and taps 'Send on Fri, 8:00 am to 12 members', the done card says 'Sent to 12 in the app', the same words as a message sent now. Nothing says it is waiting for Friday. Members without the app are put on the WhatsApp list at that moment, and the card says they are 'ready on WhatsApp', so the owner is led to send those copies days early.
expected: A message for later says it is set for that day and time ('Set for Fri, 8:00 am: 12 members in the app'), and the WhatsApp copies are offered on that day, or the card says plainly to send them then.
fix_line: Give a later message its own done words with the day and time, and hold the WhatsApp copies until then.

title: In Hinglish, answer cards, tapped ideas and one failure line stay in English
what: With Hinglish chosen, the rows inside many answer cards stay English, because the card prints each row's name as it is: 'Different members', 'Busiest hour', 'Did not renew', 'Plan ended, may still renew', 'Plans sold', 'Fees due today', 'Follow-up overdue', 'Men' and 'Women'. Tapping a Today idea or an answer's button puts an English sentence in the chat as if the owner said it ('Send a fee reminder to members who owe money'). The line shown when a save fails ('This did not save. Check the internet and try again.') has no Hinglish either.
expected: Every word the owner reads in the assistant shows in Hinglish when he picks Hinglish, the same as the rest of the card.
how_often: every answer card with rows, every tapped idea, when Hinglish is on
fix_line: Pass row names and the failure line through the Hinglish list, add the missing lines, and show a Hinglish sentence for tapped ideas.

title: Two Hinglish labels in the assistant say the wrong thing
what: In Hinglish, the box where the owner edits a message's words is labelled 'Message karo', which means 'send a message', not 'the message'. On the AI credits sheet, 'Recently used' becomes 'Haal mein', which only means 'recently' and loses that the list is what used credits. 'More polite' becomes 'Aur vinamra', a formal Hindi word few owners type.
expected: Labels mean the same in both languages: 'Message' as a field name (for example 'Message ke shabd'), 'Haal mein lage credits', and an everyday word for polite (for example 'Aur pyaar se').
fix_line: Give the message box its own Hinglish label and fix the two credit-sheet lines; he reads them aloud first.

title: History calls an unsaved member, payment or expense 'Not sent'
what: Every task in History that was written but not finished is marked 'Not sent', including adding a member, a renewal, a payment, an extension, an enquiry and an expense. Nothing is ever 'sent' for those; the owner may think a member or payment went somewhere.
expected: Unfinished changes say 'Not saved' (and messages 'Not sent'), the same words the cards use.
fix_line: Pick 'Not saved' or 'Not sent' by the kind of task.

title: The assistant gives one member's page three names, and dues two
what: After adding or renewing a member the button says 'Open Member card'; an answer about one member says 'Open their page'; an extension over the limit says 'open the member's page'. The same screen has three names. Money owed is 'Fees due' on Today ideas and in the page list, but 'Members who owe fees' opens a page called 'Dues'.
expected: One name for each screen across the assistant, matching what the menu and the screen itself say.
fix_line: Use the screen's own title everywhere: 'member's page' and 'Fees due', or rename the page list entries.

title: With member AI on and a limit of 0, the sheet says both 'members can ask 3 a day' and 'members get help pages'
what: On the AI credits sheet, when 'Members can get AI answers' is ticked and the monthly limit is 0, the line under the tick says each member can ask the AI 3 questions a day, while the line under the limit says members get help pages instead of AI answers. Both show at once; the second is what happens.
expected: When the limit is 0, the line under the tick says members get help pages, or the tick turns off by itself.
how_often: when the limit is set to 0 with the tick on
fix_line: Show the help-pages line under the tick when the limit is 0.
